names.note: The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2250, headed «Феотекн Антиохийский, мч.», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

death.note: The calendar's day line prints «ок. 284-305» and the life it reaches dates the same emperor's reign «при императоре Максимиане (305 - 311)»; the two spans overlap only at 305 and the page does not reconcile them, so the interval carries both ends.

source.note: No rank is read onto him. His line opens the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon. The day's two icons are both in the first paragraph: the plain service before the martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, and a polyeleos immediately before Ambrose of Optina.

attestations.note: He is **not** either of the two the corpus already holds under this name: `theotecnus-the-martyr`, whom the Greek keeps on 3 October and says was stoned, and `theoteknos`, whom the Greek keeps on 10 December and says was killed by the sword. This one is the commander at Antioch under Maximian, kept on the Russian 10 October and drowned with a stone round his neck. Three entries, three days, three deaths. His name page keeps him on this day and no other.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.10.2026 (10. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Теотски.“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry, and **the only upgrade of this range so far that takes no `sr` name form.** The heading is quoted whole, with the closing full stop the Prologue itself prints, which is what BRIEF-SERBIAN section 4 asks for. It had to be measured off the raw cached page, because srbody.mjs and sr-cand.mjs both strip it from their printed output: every heading of this day ends ". " in the source. **THE HEADING’S PERSONAL NAME IS «Теотски» AND THAT IS NOT A NAME THIS READER WILL ASSERT IS HIS.** The raw page prints `Св. муч. Теотски. ` — measured off the cached HTML, so it is the book’s own string and not the parser’s — and it reads as a contraction or a corruption of Теотекн, the «Феотекн» of the Russian index. **A name form is one of the nine things a machine may not decide and a reader does not mend a source’s spelling**, so the string is preserved where it belongs — inside the quoted heading of this row, exactly as printed — and no `names` entry is written off it. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for it, which is no argument either way. **Whether the Prologue’s form should be stored as it stands is the author’s.** THE IDENTIFICATION IS ON THE SCENE AND NOT ON THE NAME, which is the only way it could have been made here. The entry gives a **Roman officer at Antioch in the time of Maximian** who was **drowned in the sea with a stone about his neck after great torments**; this folder’s Russian life gives a famous military commander at Antioch under Maximian who was at last thrown into the sea with a stone round his neck. Rank, city, reign and manner of death, four things together. The folder’s own life already separates it from the Theotecnus of 3 October, who was stoned, and the Theoteknos of 10 December, who was killed with the sword; the manner of death in this entry is the drowning, which is this man’s. **THE ENTRY GIVES HIM WORDS AND NO OTHER BOOK READ FOR THIS FOLDER DOES.** When the emperor offered him the sacrifice he answered „ја верујем у Христа Бога, и Њему ћу принети на жртву себе – жртву живу.“ — I believe in Christ God, and to him I will offer myself as a sacrifice, a living sacrifice. WHAT IT DOES NOT HAVE: no women’s clothes and no spinning with the slave women, no three weeks, no burnt feet or cut tendons, no cauldron of pitch that went cold, no prison, no confessor Alexandra helped to escape and no finding of the relics on the Cilician coast. Four sentences against a page. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the folder holds `death` 284–311 and **this entry prints no year**, dating him only by Maximian — an emperor is not a source for a year. `types` untouched at `martyr`, `soldier`: муч. in the heading is the `martyr`, and «Официр римски» corroborates the `soldier` the Russian life gave. No `office` — a Roman commission is not an ecclesiastical office. `related` UNTOUCHED and the folder has none: the entry names nobody but the emperor. No `locations`. **THIS IS THE FOLDER’S SECOND CALENDAR**, which is worth saying because the Russian was its only venerated row until now. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. TWO REFUSALS ON THIS DAY, BOTH ON SECTION 4’S GROUND, AND BOTH ARE WORTH THE NEXT READER’S TIME. **(1) The day’s second entry is refused whole.** Its heading is «Св. мученици Зографски.» and **it enumerates nobody**. The body tells the burning of the tower of Zographou by the Latin troops Michael VIII Palaiologos brought to Athos after the Union of Lyon, counts the dead as twenty-six — twenty-two monks with their abbot and four laymen who worked for the house — names the abbot Тома, and dates it 10 October 1283. **The corpus already keeps about twenty-six Zographou folders on this menologion day**, `thomas-of-zographou` among them. A synaxis heading that names nobody is one entry and the reader says so; counting by section 5 means counting what the heading enumerates and not what the body narrates, which is the ground two named martyrs were refused rows on earlier in this wave. So **no row went to any Zographou folder**. Two things in it are the author’s: whether that heading warrants twenty-six rows, and that the entry gives the burning as **1283** where `thomas-of-zographou` holds `death` 1275–1282 — a year outside the folder’s interval, offered by an entry that takes no row, so nothing was widened on it. **(2) `two-hundred-martyrs-of-nicomedia` is refused a row.** The first entry ends «Још бише погублени 200 хришћана» — two hundred more Christians were put to death, who believed on seeing the power and the wonders of the two — and the Greek calendar keeps those two hundred as an entry of their own on this same day, which is why the folder exists and why both of this entry’s folders already relate it. **But the Prologue narrates them inside a body whose heading names only Евлампије and Евлампија**, and a row’s quoted line is the heading, whole. No row, and the reason is named rather than left to look like an oversight.
